title: Europe sees surge in suspected Russian hybrid warfare incidents
gist: Early November 2026 brought bomb threats against airports (Rome, Copenhagen, Prague, Warsaw, Lisbon) and broadcasters plus a multi-country cyberattack on supermarket freezer systems, all suspected but unproven Russian hybrid operations. The text's author (Maksym Beznosiuk, though raw author is Peter Dickinson) argues Russia is shifting to civilian-disruption ops designed to avoid attribution and erode European support for Ukraine, and Europe should prepare for a prolonged campaign.

insights.claim: A series of bomb threats in early November 2026 disrupted air travel at airports in Rome, Copenhagen, Prague, Warsaw and Lisbon, and also targeted broadcasters including RTÉ and Sky News; European agencies are probing Russian involvement.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Recurring airport disruptions are an operational risk for European airlines and airports.
insights.locator: Air travel across the continent was disrupted

insights.claim: A large-scale cyber operation targeted frozen food section systems at supermarket chains across multiple European countries, causing millions of dollars of damage and temporary food supply issues, with security experts citing hallmarks of Russian hybrid warfare.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: European retailers' operational-technology (refrigeration) systems are an attack surface — supports demand for OT cybersecurity.
insights.quote: a spate of cyberattacks targeting the frozen food sections of supermarkets across Europe

insights.claim: The attempted Russian bombing of Leipzig Airport in August 2026 was widely seen as a watershed marking a dangerous new phase in the Kremlin's shadow war.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Escalation from disruption to attempted kinetic sabotage on EU soil raises security costs for European infrastructure operators.
insights.locator: Over the course of the past year

insights.claim: Over the past year, suspected Russian hybrid attacks escalated markedly, including more frequent NATO airspace violations by Russian drones, strikes on Black Sea shipping, and sabotage of infrastructure across Europe.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Rising Black Sea shipping and infrastructure risk feeds insurance premia and European defense/security spending.
insights.locator: Over the course of the past year

insights.claim: European officials may never be able to prove Russia is behind these incidents, because the operations are designed to avoid attribution and stay below the threshold of interstate hostilities.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Lack of attribution limits formal retaliation, so expect the campaign to continue without clear escalation triggers.
insights.quote: specifically designed to avoid attribution and remain below the recognized threshold for interstate hostilities
insights.locator: In reality, there is a good chance

insights.claim: Russia maintains plausible deniability by combining cyber capabilities, criminal intermediaries, and disposable agents recruited via Telegram and social media, which also compensates for mass expulsions of conventional Russian agents from the West.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Gig-style sabotage recruitment via social platforms creates regulatory pressure on platforms like Telegram.
insights.quote: disposable agents recruited through Telegram and other social media platforms

insights.claim: The widely assumed but deniable Russian responsibility suits Moscow because it shapes European public opinion about the domestic security costs of supporting Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: The goal is political: watch European polling on Ukraine aid as the metric Moscow is targeting.
insights.quote: Russia’s hybrid war against Europe is widely regarded as an open secret. This suits Moscow just fine.
insights.locator: While the Kremlin inevitably denies everything

themes.theme: Strategic shift: targeting civilian daily life

insights.claim: Recent incidents mark a shift toward disrupting ordinary civilians' daily lives — flight delays and food access — to create insecurity among Europeans who do not feel militarily threatened by Russia.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Civilian-facing critical infrastructure (aviation, retail, logistics) is the new target set; resilience spending should rise.
insights.locator: The most recent incidents signal a shift

insights.claim: With Russia's army unable to secure a battlefield breakthrough, the Kremlin's new plan pairs bombing Ukraine's civilian infrastructure with intensified hybrid war to scare European backers into abandoning Kyiv.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Two-front pressure (Ukraine grid + European hybrid) is the Kremlin's winter strategy.
insights.locator: Russia’s campaign of gray zone hostilities

insights.claim: Russia's gray-zone campaign is expected to escalate in coming months, and Europe should prepare for prolonged hybrid hostilities threatening all kinds of civilian infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Supports sustained demand for European cybersecurity, critical-infrastructure protection and defense spending.
insights.quote: Europe should prepare for a prolonged campaign of hybrid hostilities that poses a threat to civilian infrastructure of all kinds
insights.locator: European leaders appear to be taking this threat
